title: Ada and the Current
premise: Paloma Kavanagh flies supply runs into the remote interior, keeping her head down to pay off a debt she inherited from her late father. When a government survey team vanishes near a river the locals call the Current, she is the only pilot willing to search, and what she finds—survivors, sealed instruments, and readings that shouldn't exist—makes her the unwilling keeper of a secret the government will kill to contain. Torn between her growing love for Elian, a survey geologist who remembers nothing of the last three days, and her duty to deliver the team home intact and silent, Paloma must choose between obedience and truth. In the end she burns the survey's findings mid-flight over the Current, turning herself in to save Elian, and discovers that belonging means being seen—even at the cost of everything she flew in with.
about_author: Gideon Hartwell is the pen name of a former bush mechanic who spent six years servicing airstrips across the northern interior before trading wrenches for words. He writes adventure fiction about people who live where maps run out.

chapters.title: Fuel, Debt, and Weather
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A routine medicine run establishes her world: the aging Beaver aircraft, the ledger of her father's debt pinned above the instrument panel, and the small community that trusts her but knows little of her. She refuses a charter request from a government survey outfit, wanting no official eyes on her routes. Emotional beat: guarded independence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Quiet Frequency
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Radio chatter from the survey camp goes silent mid-transmission; then a garbled mayday names coordinates inside a canyon no chart marks correctly. The regional office asks her to look, since she's the only pilot rated for that strip. She finds the camp intact—tents pitched, kettle warm—but eleven people gone, tracks ending abruptly at the riverbank. Emotional beat: dread arriving quietly.

chapters.title: Gear With No Tracks
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, shifting briefly to Elian's fragmented memories. She lands and searches: sealed instrument cases, a recorder still running, and one survivor—Elian—wandering the shoreline with three days missing from his mind. He doesn't remember her, though he insists they've met. Emotional beat: uncanny connection amid mystery.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. Recovering aboard Paloma's plane en route to the nearest town, Elian recalls flashes: humming water, lights beneath the Current, his team walking into it willingly. He hides this from Paloma, ashamed and afraid. Meanwhile she notices government aircraft already circling the canyon. Emotional beat: intimacy built on concealment.

chapters.title: The Man From the Ministry
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A smooth official named Corrigan meets them on the strip, offering to erase Paloma's debt in exchange for silence and the recovered instruments. She hands over the cases but keeps the recorder, an instinct she can't explain. That night Elian admits he remembers her—from a stopover two years ago neither should recall so vividly. Emotional beat: temptation versus trust.

chapters.title: Debt Paid in Full
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Corrigan makes good: her father's ledger is cleared, but the price becomes clear when she learns the other ten survey members were never lost—they were recovered days ago and signed secrecy oaths, leaving Elian as the loose end. If he remembers too much, he'll be handled. Emotional beat: freedom that feels like a trap.

chapters.title: Three Days Under
chapters.summary: Elian's POV. Under pressure to sign the oath, Elian fights to reconstruct the missing days, realizing the Current showed each team member something they'd lost—a memory, a person, a home—and that he saw Paloma. Duty says sign; love says refuse. He tears up the oath and goes to her. Emotional beat: choosing feeling over safety.

chapters.title: Running the Canyon
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. With Corrigan's men moving to detain Elian, the pair flee in the Beaver at dawn, low through fog, chased by a faster government plane. Paloma realizes the only leverage left is the recorder—the full record of what the Current found them. Emotional beat: terror sharpened by resolve.

chapters.title: Over the Current
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, climax. Cornered over the canyon with fuel bleeding away, Paloma must decide: trade the recorder for their lives, or destroy the findings and let the Current keep its secret. She opens the window and drops the recorder into the water below; the pursuing plane peels off, its mission void. Emotional beat: sacrifice as liberation.

chapters.title: A Place on the Map
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs, resolution. Weeks later, stripped of her license pending inquiry, Paloma expects exile—but the interior communities rally, vouching for her, and Elian stays on as the settlement's reluctant teacher of things half-remembered. Flying again under a local charter, she pins no debt above the panel, only a photo. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not inherited.
